Thirty-seventh is "Flaying the Skin."
The ghosts constantly use sharp knives to flay their skin;
harboring evil intentions, they strip people of their clothing and robes,
as well as the skins of various sentient beings.
In future births among humans, they will constantly be robbed and plundered by others.
Thirty-eighth is "Hanging Upside Down":
the hell-wardens take the people and hang them upside down.
At birth, sentient beings are born upside down.
Thirty-nine is the realm of animals;
in hell, ghosts have molten copper poured into their mouths.
If one evades and does not repay a debt,
in the final five hundred years they will become a human being’s ox, horse, slave, or servant.
They joyfully receive flogging.
The forty days are called "plowing the body":
the hell-demons plow their bodies with iron plows.
While plowing fields at birth, he injured sentient beings;
with an evil mind, he uttered a curse.
The forty-first is called *Cakṣuḥ-śalya* (Eye-Spear).
The hell-demons constantly pierce their eyes with iron barbs.
Because they looked upon their parents with evil hearts and evil eyes during their lifetime,
when they are later reborn among humans, their eyes are always crossed.
Forty-second is the calamity of weapons.
The hell-ghosts hack and shoot;
these people, during their lifetime, killed one another with hearts of hatred.
Those born subsequently among humans will frequently suffer from being cut and pierced.
The forty-third is called "Cutting and Piercing," wherein the hell-wardens slice off their flesh while they are alive.
When this person was alive, they maliciously cut the flesh of others;
when their retribution is exhausted, they become a human who delights in cutting and piercing.
The forty-fourth is called Iron Grinding.
The hell-wardens grind people with iron mills.
When these people were alive, they used their evil minds to grind to death insects; therefore, they are ground here.
The forty-fifth [hell] is called *Zhunong* (Torturing).
The hells are filled with iron grinders.
The hell-wardens drive the inhabitants into these grinders to be crushed.
Forty-sixth is the Hell of Tossing and Twisting.
When this person was born,
they saw sentient beings being subjected to mockery and torture,
and gave rise to an evil thought, vowing: "I shall never save them."
In their subsequent births among humans, their bodies will be jaundiced and withered.
Forty-seventh is the Stone Mortar:
they are suddenly driven into a mortar and pounded there.
When this person was alive, they crushed and killed sentient beings with an evil mind;
when their retribution is exhausted, they become a snail or a clam. Forty-eight: Arrogance.
Human head with a serpent’s body.
When this person was alive, they would lie on the ground while reciting sutras.
On the forty-ninth day, they enter the Water Hell.
The water remains stagnant and does not flow.
When this person was alive, they suppressed others in water so that they drowned and died.
The fiftyth is called *Yurou*.
The hell-demon presses the person's head with a stone.
During this person's lifetime, their arrogance caused their parents and teachers to be treated as mere props.
It causes their children to speak with irreverence.
The fifty-first is called the Iron Club:
the hell-demons constantly cause iron clubs to strike the bodies of those who, during their lifetime, killed lice and nits with malicious intent.
Fifty-second is "Terror":
one is constantly terrified by the ox-headed *ābhas* demons.
Because this person was constantly fearful of others during their lifetime, [they now suffer this retribution].
Fifty-three is called the Iron Stake Hell.
Iron stakes are laid out at the bottom of the water;
the hell-demons drive the inhabitants into the water so that their bodies are pierced and blood flows.
Fifty-fourth: Drinking molten copper. In one's lifetime, with a mind of arrogance, one mimicked the speech of parents, teachers, and elders.
Thereafter, he will always be stammering and halting.
The fifty-fifth is called Iron Arrowhead:
the hell-demons pierce his eyes with iron arrowheads.
When this person was born, their evil mind pierced the pupils of sentient beings;
when their retribution is exhausted, they become blind.
The fifty-sixth is called the Iron Fist Hell (Ayaḥmuṣṭi-naraka).
The hell-guardians strike people with iron clubs.
This person, while alive, struck fish and other sentient beings with an evil mind.
Fifty-seven is named "Worms."
They devour human bodies.
While these people are alive, they cause harm through maggots and jealousy toward humans,
as well as toward domestic animals and property.
When their retribution is completed, they become human beings afflicted with malignant sores.
Fifty-eight is called "Hands Severed by Knife":
the hell-demons use sharp knives to sever both their hands.
When this person was born, they grasped the sutras with hands that were impure due to pride;
on the fifty-ninth day, they wept.
The hell-demons seize him and terrify him, causing him to wail and weep.
During his life, this person was constantly anxious about wealth for the sake of pursuing sensual pleasures;
consequently, when reborn as a human, he suffers perpetually from a lack of resources.
The sixtieth is called Iron Shackles.
The hell-demons constantly bind the bodies of those in this realm with iron shackles;
these individuals, while alive, used shackles to kill sentient beings.
The sixty-first is Molten Copper.
The hell-demons pour molten copper into the mouths of these beings;
this was because they harbored evil intentions during their lifetimes.
For those who have committed false speech, slander, harsh abuse, and frivolous chatter,
their breath shall perpetually stink once their retribution is complete.
The sixty-second [retribution] is having molten copper poured upon one's hands.
When this person was born, their mind did not revere the Path.
They grasped the robe of a śramaṇa with unclean hands.
The sixty-third [hell] is called Shooting the Body.
The hell-wardens shoot him with arrows.
This person, during his lifetime, harbored an evil mind and shot and killed living beings.
Sixty-fourth: "No-choice" (Avīci); in the language of Liang, this means that from birth until death, there are generally five kings.
The first is called King Anu;
the second is called King Kalpa;
the third is called King Virūpa.
The fourth is called the Natural King;
the fifth is called the Sentient-Being King.
Both have given rise to the faith and Mahāyāna vows to deliver sentient beings from the hells.
Those whose karmic retributions for the various hells have been exhausted enter this realm.
Their past conduct and the extent of the sins they committed are severed;
they cast off their hellish bodies and assume the form of an intermediate state being (*antarābhava*) resembling a three-year-old child.
Furthermore, following the karmic actions [of beings], they are born from their parents;
this is the *Sūtra on Questions Concerning the Arising in Hell*. 4. The Five Great Earth Hells Showing the Signs of Suffering. The Four Earth Hells of Revival.
With malicious minds, they quarrel and contend, piercing one another with spears;
they claw at each other with iron talons until their bodies are smeared and drenched in blood.
Tormented by agonizing pain, they become so faint that they lose all consciousness.
When a cold wind blows,
the hell-wardens call out to the living offenders, and they return to life;
therefore, it is called the Reviving Hell (Saṃjīva).
Among these beings, there were those who in previous lives delighted in killing living creatures— cattle, sheep, birds, and beasts—
for the sake of fields, houses, kingdoms, lands, wealth, and other such interests, slaying one another;
they now undergo this retribution for their sins.
In the Great Universal Hell,
rākṣasa hell-wardens assume various forms with the heads of diverse malevolent beasts.
They come to swallow, devour, and gnaw upon the sinners;
two mountains close together and crush them with hot iron wheels,
while they are pounded in hot iron mortars as if oil were being pressed.
Heaps of flesh form mounds and streams of blood form pools.
Vultures, eagles, tigers, and wolves each come to pull and drag [the body].
This person, having killed many sentient beings in previous lives, now undergoes this physical form in hell as retribution.
Furthermore, by using force and power to oppress and crush the weak,
one incurs the retribution of being caught between two converging mountains;
likewise for those who harbor stinginess, greed, anger, delusion, and fear.
When adjudicating legal cases, they do not employ correct principles,
or they subvert the right path; consequently,
they receive the punishment of being crushed by a glowing iron wheel and pounded in an iron mortar.
The fourth and fifth are named Raurava and Mahāraurava. Within these great hells,
the rakshasa wardens have yellow necks and red eyes, from which fire issues forth.
Clad in crimson robes, his body was firm and powerful;
he ran and shot at the sinners, who,
overcome with frantic terror, knelt and begged for mercy.
"O Great General, have some small measure of compassion!
We are being led into the Hot Iron Hell,
which is one hundred yojanas in length and breadth."
Driven and beaten, they are driven away until their feet are completely scorched;
fat and marrow flow out like pressed sesame oil,
and from the heads and foreheads struck by iron clubs, the brains stream forth like broken jars of curd.
Furthermore, they are led into the interior of an iron chamber where black smoke billows forth to suffocate them;
pressing against one another, they long to find a way out.
The gates are already closed, yet the sound of loud wailing and crying never ceases.
This person, in his previous life, deceived others with false scales and measures;
he adjudicated matters unjustly and failed to return items entrusted to him.
They oppress the lowly and afflict the poor, causing them to wail;
they destroy cities and ruin villages,
harming and plundering until the entire city cries out in distress.
Deceiving them into coming forth and then harming them,
one now undergoes the Scream of Wailing Hell;
by fumigating and killing those who dwell in burrows, one is confined within a prison.
Some are suffocated by smoke within dark caves;
others are cast into wells to plunder the wealth of others—
all such persons receive the retributive punishment of the Great Howling Hell.
In the sixth and seventh hells, Tapana and Pratāpana,
there are two great copper cauldrons filled with brackish, boiling water.
The rākṣasas and hell-wardens cast the sinners into it;
their feet are up and their heads down, and their bones and joints fall apart.
As they are pierced by iron skewers, a cold wind blows them back to life, and they are cast once more into the pit of burning coals.
Or they are cast into boiling ashes;
emerging from the ashes, they are placed amidst hot sand,
where they are further seared and scorched by pus and blood.
Emerging from the charcoal pit, they are thrown onto a bed of flames and forcibly driven to sit.
From their eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and all their pores, fire erupts.
This is because in past lives this person troubled and disturbed their parents, teachers, elders, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and all virtuous people.
Affliction causes the mind to burn, and now one receives the retribution of the Heat Hell.
Perhaps in a previous life one boiled and killed silkworm cocoons,
or was born as a rotting pig or sheep.
Some pierce people’s bellies with wooden stakes and roast them alive;
some burn mountains, forests, villages, Buddhist temples, monasteries, and deva shrines;
or they push sentient beings into pits of fire.
Therefore, they are born in this hell.
The Avīci Hell is four thousand li in length and breadth;
its location is the deepest of all.
The rākṣasa wardens flay the skin from his head down to his feet;
they nail his body with five hundred spikes as if stretching a hide of ox-hide,
and tread upon him with hot iron chariots.
They are driven into pits of fire and forced to carry out burning coals;
sharp swords, blades, and spears fly into their bodies, leaving them dazed, fainting, and withered;
some fall prostrate in their distress.
This person, due to their past conduct, has committed many great evils.
Having incurred the grave offenses of the five heinous crimes and severed their roots of goodness,
they declare the Dharma to be non-Dharma and non-Dharma to be the Dharma.

Those who deny cause and effect and harbor malice toward virtuous people enter this hell, where they undergo the most severe punishments; I have extracted from the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* those points that are most striking, omitting minor similarities.
